newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish men detained over shooting of policewoman.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish men detained over shooting of policewoman.

text.p: Several men were arrested in early morning police raids in the Northern Ireland city of Londonderry for questioning about guerrilla crime, security sources said on Wednesday.

The suspects, detained in two Irish nationalist housing zones, were arrested by officers probing an IRA sniper attack that seriously wounded a policewoman in the city last month, according to the sources.
"A number of men were arrested at their homes in the Bogside and Galliagh areas. They are being questioned about recent terrorist crime," said a Royal Ulster Constabulary spokesman.
Policewoman Alice Collins, 46, a mother of three, was shot in the back by an Irish Republican Army sniper while she was on guard duty near Londonderrry's heavily protected courthouse on April 10.
The IRA has not launched attacks in the province since then but planted bombs to disrupt England's transport system in the six-week approach to Britain's general election last Thursday.
British troops defused an under-car booby trap bomb at a Catholic nationalist area in north Belfast early on Wednesday, police sources said.
Late on Tuesday, police intercepted a suspected van bomb near a Belfast concert hall where Britain's Prince Charles was attending a gala function, but it turned out to be a hoax.

Police alerted British bomb disposal experts who carried out two precautionary controlled explosions at the vehicle. It had been hijacked in a Catholic district by masked men who ordered the driver to take it to the concert hall.
The incidents were the latest to heighten tension in British-ruled Northern Ireland in recent months.
Despite the uneasy lull in IRA attacks, security forces have remained on high alert against the guerrillas who are trying to end British sovereignty in the province.
No group claimed Wednesday's foiled under-car bombing. Protestant extremists loyal to Britain have launched several bomb attacks reportedly in revenge for the IRA's wave of disruption in England.

Multi-party talks on the province's future are due to restart on June 3. Britain and Ireland say that the IRA's Sinn Fein political wing will not be admitted until the Irish guerrillas abandon violence.
